fields.label: FAQ 1: Answer
fields.name: faq1Answer
fields.default_value: Legacy application modernization is the process of upgrading or transforming outdated software applications into modern, secure, scalable, and maintainable systems. It encompasses code refactoring, architecture redesign, cloud migration, database modernization, API integration, or complete application reengineering.

fields.label: FAQ 2: Question
fields.name: faq2Question
fields.default_value: How does AI help modernize legacy applications?

fields.label: FAQ 2: Answer
fields.name: faq2Answer
fields.default_value: AI helps modernize legacy applications by assisting with source code analysis, dependency discovery, code refactoring, documentation generation, test creation, and software transformation. Generative AI and intelligent development tools reduce repetitive engineering work and accelerate modernization activities by up to 60%.

fields.label: FAQ 3: Question
fields.name: faq3Question
fields.default_value: What is AI-powered legacy application modernization?

fields.label: FAQ 3: Answer
fields.name: faq3Answer
fields.default_value: AI-powered legacy application modernization uses artificial intelligence, Generative AI, and intelligent automation to assist with analyzing, transforming, testing, and upgrading outdated software systems. It pairs AI-assisted engineering with experienced software architects to maximize transformation speed while ensuring total code quality.

fields.label: FAQ 4: Question
fields.name: faq4Question
fields.default_value: How does Hutech modernize legacy applications?

fields.label: FAQ 4: Answer
fields.name: faq4Answer
fields.default_value: Hutech modernizes legacy applications through a disciplined 5-step methodology: application assessment, modernization strategy selection (7 Rs), AI-assisted code transformation, cloud reengineering, automated testing, and zero-downtime deployment. We leverage our proprietary Agentic Development Platform for automated AST analysis and test generation.

fields.label: FAQ 5: Question
fields.name: faq5Question
fields.default_value: What is Agentic AI in application modernization?

fields.label: FAQ 5: Answer
fields.name: faq5Answer
fields.default_value: Agentic AI in application modernization refers to using specialized AI agents to autonomously execute discrete software engineering tasks—such as parsing legacy ASTs, identifying business rules, refactoring code syntax, generating documentation, and writing comprehensive test suites—all governed and approved by senior human engineers.

fields.label: FAQ 6: Question
fields.name: faq6Question
fields.default_value: Can AI convert legacy code into modern programming languages?

fields.label: FAQ 6: Answer
fields.name: faq6Answer
fields.default_value: Yes, AI can assist developers in translating, restructuring, and refactoring legacy code into modern languages (such as COBOL to Java, or .NET Framework to .NET 8). However, AI-generated code must always undergo architectural validation and automated comparison testing to ensure 100% business logic equivalence.

fields.label: FAQ 7: Question
fields.name: faq7Question
fields.default_value: Can legacy monolithic applications be converted into microservices?

fields.label: FAQ 7: Answer
fields.name: faq7Answer
fields.default_value: Yes. We use the proven Strangler Fig pattern combined with Domain-Driven Design (DDD). We map bounded contexts, establish an API gateway, and incrementally extract microservices one domain at a time, ensuring continuous production operations throughout the transformation.

fields.label: FAQ 8: Question
fields.name: faq8Question
fields.default_value: What are the benefits of modernizing legacy applications?

fields.label: FAQ 8: Answer
fields.name: faq8Answer
fields.default_value: Modernizing legacy applications eliminates technical debt, reduces infrastructure costs by up to 50%, removes security vulnerabilities, improves application uptime, enables elastic cloud scaling, and reduces new feature delivery cycles from months to days.

fields.label: FAQ 9: Question
fields.name: faq9Question
fields.default_value: How long does legacy application modernization take?

fields.label: FAQ 9: Answer
fields.name: faq9Answer
fields.default_value: Timelines depend on application complexity, lines of code, dependencies, and chosen strategy. A targeted refactoring or replatforming can take 8–16 weeks, while large-scale enterprise core system reengineering may take 6–12 months in phased iterative releases.

fields.label: FAQ 10: Question
fields.name: faq10Question
fields.default_value: What is the difference between application modernization and application migration?

fields.label: FAQ 10: Answer
fields.name: faq10Answer
fields.default_value: Application migration primarily involves moving an application from one environment (such as on-premise) to another (the cloud) with minimal code changes (rehosting). Application modernization fundamentally transforms the application's code, architecture, data layer, and operations to be cloud-native and maintainable.

fields.label: FAQ 11: Question
fields.name: faq11Question
fields.default_value: How does Hutech's Agentic Development Platform support modernization?

fields.label: FAQ 11: Answer
fields.name: faq11Answer
fields.default_value: Hutech's Agentic Development Platform orchestrates intelligent workflows for AST code parsing, dependency graph extraction, automated documentation generation, automated test harness creation, and syntax refactoring, eliminating manual drudgery while keeping human engineers in command.

fields.label: FAQ 12: Question
fields.name: faq12Question
fields.default_value: How can organizations reduce risks during legacy modernization?

fields.label: FAQ 12: Answer
fields.name: faq12Answer
fields.default_value: Risk is mitigated through thorough upfront discovery, phased incremental migration (never big-bang), behavioral parity testing comparing legacy and modern outputs with real production payloads, automated rollback strategies, and strict human review.

fields.label: FAQ 13: Question
fields.name: faq13Question
fields.default_value: What is the best strategy for modernizing legacy applications?

fields.label: FAQ 13: Answer
fields.name: faq13Answer
fields.default_value: The best strategy depends on business value, architectural health, and operational constraints. We evaluate applications across Gartner's 7 Rs (Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Rearchitect, Rebuild, Replace, Retain/Retire) to recommend the optimal balance of speed, cost, and long-term agility.

fields.label: FAQ 14: Question
fields.name: faq14Question
fields.default_value: Can legacy applications be modernized without disrupting business operations?

fields.label: FAQ 14: Answer
fields.name: faq14Answer
fields.default_value: Yes. Through blue/green deployments, canary releases, database dual-writing/synchronization, and the Strangler Fig pattern, business operations remain live and uninterrupted while underlying components are upgraded transparently.

fields.label: FAQ 15: Question
fields.name: faq15Question
fields.default_value: How do I get started with legacy application modernization?

fields.label: FAQ 15: Answer
fields.name: faq15Answer
fields.default_value: Get started by requesting an AI-Powered Modernization Assessment from Hutech. Our architects will analyze your source repositories, map technical debt, identify quick wins, and present an actionable transformation roadmap.
